name: Twenty-Twentiers — The Collapse Nostalgia Scene
creator: Diffuse origin; crystallized around the Coldframe-adjacent stylist collective Ashfall Drift, 2201-2209
description: A sustained retro fashion movement fixated on the aesthetic of the 2020s-2040s — the pre-Collapse decades immediately preceding the nation-state failures — characterized by fast-fashion silhouettes, logo-heavy branding from defunct corporate entities, synthetic fiber palettes in muted earth tones and oversaturated neons, and deliberate technological primitivism in accessories (non-BCI-integrated jewelry, non-conductive fabrics, analog fasteners). Practitioners called themselves Twenty-Twentiers and wore the era's clothing as a form of grief-cosplay, mourning a world most of them only knew from archived neural feeds. The movement had a deeply ambivalent relationship with the violence of that period — some wearers treated the aesthetic as ironic memorial, others as genuine longing for a simpler pre-augmentation world.
medium: physical garments, vintage and reproduction pieces, neural feed styling channels, gray-market archive drops
cultural_impact: Reignited debate about pre-Collapse cultural memory and who has the right to nostalgize a period that killed millions; also became an unexpected entry point for anti-augmentation sentiment, since 2020s fashion was definitionally non-chrome, giving Rawskin and Flatskin movements a visual vocabulary.
controversy: Corponation historians and Axiom-aligned cultural commentators accused Twenty-Twentiers of romanticizing the nation-state era and implicitly critiquing the Sable Charter. Several Shelf critics pointed out that the 2020s-2040s were catastrophic for the communities whose descendants now live on the Shelf, making the nostalgia tone-deaf at best. A counter-movement called Collapse Honest emerged briefly, producing Twenty-Twentier-adjacent clothing deliberately stained, torn, and marked with Collapse-era casualty data.
story_hooks: A Twenty-Twentier collector acquires what she believes is an original 2031 garment from a Shelf estate sale — the provenance trail leads to a family that died in the Lachine Corridor collapse, and the garment still carries BCI-readable emotional residue.

A Tier 4 corponation launches an officially licensed 'Collapse Chic' collection, co-opting the Twenty-Twentier aesthetic and triggering a schism in the movement between purists and those who take the licensing money.

A Shelf teenager who cannot afford reproduction pieces begins wearing her actual grandmother's surviving 2030s clothing to school — and becomes involuntarily iconic when a neural feed stylist photographs her without consent.
